target_customer: ML teams at autonomous vehicle, robotics and computer vision companies
problem: Model performance is limited by dataset quality, and teams lack tools to find label errors, anomalies and failure patterns in training data. Aquarium surfaced these and helped teams fix them.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for ML dataset tooling
product_category: ML data curation and dataset debugging

founders.name: Peter Gao
founders.background_notes: Early employee and perception tech lead at Cruise.

founders.name: Quinn Johnson
founders.background_notes: First engineering hire at Graphistry; met Gao at Cruise.

exit.reason: Company said its retrieval technology complemented Notion's AI plans; products were shut down and team joined Notion's AI group.

competitors.name: Scale Nucleus
competitors.what: Dataset management product tied to Scale AI labeling
competitors.funding_then: Scale AI was a well-funded labeling company

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed embedding-based search, visualization and large dataset handling for image and point cloud data; hard parts were scale and ML expertise but not research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Labeling vendors and MLOps platforms could add similar features; customer workflow integration gave only mild lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Scale launched Nucleus in August 2020, the same month as the batch; Aquarium was ultimately acquired by Notion, which shut down its original products.

market_need_then: Self-driving and computer vision teams were spending heavily on labeling and found data quality was the main bottleneck, a point of rising attention in 2020 as data-centric AI emerged.

branding.domain_note: Operated as aquariumlearning.com, not a bare aquarium .com.

brand_strength.rationale: Brand mostly invisible in search results, which are dominated by physical aquariums; no sources on mascot or community.

outcome_analysis: Aquarium was founded by two Cruise alumni who understood data problems in self-driving, raised a $2.6M Sequoia-led seed in February 2021 and had no reported later round. It was absorbed into Notion's AI team in 2024 and the products were shut down, which reads as a team and technology acquisition rather than a scaled outcome, with the price undisclosed.
notes: Funding completeness inferred from TechCrunch plus CB Insights showing $2.73M over three rounds, including a small YC amount of $125K reported by an aggregator but not recorded. Acquisition year 2024 comes from Sequoia's company page; the Notion announcement date was not confirmed. Deal terms not found.
